description: Multi-class discovery: ID derivation, snake_case conversion, conflict detection, and backward compatibility (PROTOCOL_SPEC §2.1.1). Opt-in is the per-class `multi_class` marker (D-107, spec v1.50.0); the file-level `multi_class_enabled` input these cases used to carry was the toggle decision-log D-06 withdrew, and pinning it kept all three SDKs passing against a model the spec says does not exist.

test_cases.description: A file with exactly one Module class must produce the base_id unchanged, regardless of multi_class mode
Two Module classes in one file each receive a distinct ID with the correct snake_case class segment appended
Class name 'Addition' converts to snake_case segment 'addition'
Class name 'MathOps' converts to snake_case segment 'math_ops'
Class name 'HTTPSender' converts to snake_case segment 'http_sender'
Two classes in the same file that produce the same snake_case segment must raise MODULE_ID_CONFLICT; no modules from the file are registered
A single Module class in a deeply nested file yields the bare base_id (single-class identity guarantee), which must conform to the canonical_id grammar ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*)*$
With multi_class disabled (default), a file with two Module classes is treated as a single-class file; the base_id is returned and the second class is ignored or an SDK-policy error is raised

expected.note: Only the first qualifying class is loaded in single-class mode; the second is silently ignored or causes an error per SDK policy. The base_id is never suffixed.

test_cases.description: D-147: once a file opts in, only the classes that carry the per-class marker receive IDs. This is the case the per-class model exists for (D-107): two participating classes beside a helper class that implements the Module interface but must not become a module. An implementation that gives every qualifying class an ID once any is marked registers `math.math_ops.helper` too; one that stops registering anything from a file with an unmarked class loses the two modules.

D-147: a marked class's ID is always base_id.segment, whatever the number of marked classes, so marking a second class later never renames the first. The file has two Module classes, so the single-class identity rule (2.1.1 rule 5) does not apply. apcore-python dropped the unmarked class and then gave the one survivor the bare base_id.
